betaMC: Example Using the PCorMC Function

Ivan Jacob Agaloos Pesigan

Source: vignettes/example-p-cor-mc.Rmd
example-p-cor-mc.Rmd

Confidence intervals for squared partial correlation coefficients are generated using the PCorMC() function from the betaMC package. In this example, we use the data set and the model used in betaMC: Example Using the BetaMC Function.

library(package = betaMC)
df <- betaMC::nas1982

Regression

Fit the regression model using the lm() function.

object <- stats::lm(formula = QUALITY ~ NARTIC + PCTGRT + PCTSUPP, data = df)

Monte Carlo Sampling Distribution of Parameters

Normal-Theory Approach 

mvn <- MC(object = object, type = "mvn")

Asymptotic distribution-free Approach 

adf <- MC(object = object, type = "adf")

Heteroskedasticity Consistent Approach (HC3) 

hc3 <- MC(object = object, type = "hc3")

Squared Partial Correlation Coefficients

Normal-Theory Approach 

mvn <- PCorMC(object = mvn)

Asymptotic distribution-free Approach 

adf <- PCorMC(object = adf)

Heteroskedasticity Consistent Approach (HC3) 

hc3 <- PCorMC(object = hc3)

Methods

summary

Summary of the results of PCorMC().

summary(object = mvn)
#> Call:
#> PCorMC(object = mvn)
#> 
#> Squared partial correlations
#> type = "mvn"
#>            est     se     R  0.05%   0.5%   2.5%  97.5%  99.5% 99.95%
#> NARTIC  0.4874 0.1049 20000 0.1187 0.1847 0.2440 0.6547 0.7079 0.7669
#> PCTGRT  0.3757 0.1066 20000 0.0556 0.0970 0.1490 0.5602 0.6247 0.6820
#> PCTSUPP 0.2254 0.0989 20000 0.0053 0.0188 0.0486 0.4258 0.4988 0.5942
summary(object = adf)
#> Call:
#> PCorMC(object = adf)
#> 
#> Squared partial correlations
#> type = "adf"
#>            est     se     R  0.05%   0.5%   2.5%  97.5%  99.5% 99.95%
#> NARTIC  0.4874 0.1000 20000 0.0531 0.1566 0.2389 0.6329 0.6854 0.7525
#> PCTGRT  0.3757 0.1009 20000 0.0252 0.0899 0.1450 0.5355 0.5905 0.6601
#> PCTSUPP 0.2254 0.1034 20000 0.0004 0.0101 0.0364 0.4339 0.5023 0.5826
summary(object = hc3)
#> Call:
#> PCorMC(object = hc3)
#> 
#> Squared partial correlations
#> type = "hc3"
#>            est     se     R  0.05%   0.5%   2.5%  97.5%  99.5% 99.95%
#> NARTIC  0.4874 0.1184 20000 0.0101 0.0747 0.1814 0.6482 0.7078 0.7726
#> PCTGRT  0.3757 0.1150 20000 0.0068 0.0479 0.1073 0.5532 0.6161 0.6846
#> PCTSUPP 0.2254 0.1139 20000 0.0001 0.0034 0.0248 0.4580 0.5452 0.6468

coef

Return the vector of estimates.

stats::coef(object = mvn)
#>    NARTIC    PCTGRT   PCTSUPP 
#> 0.4874382 0.3757383 0.2253739
stats::coef(object = adf)
#>    NARTIC    PCTGRT   PCTSUPP 
#> 0.4874382 0.3757383 0.2253739
stats::coef(object = hc3)
#>    NARTIC    PCTGRT   PCTSUPP 
#> 0.4874382 0.3757383 0.2253739

vcov

Return the sampling covariance matrix.

stats::vcov(object = mvn)
#>               NARTIC       PCTGRT      PCTSUPP
#> NARTIC  0.0110141845 6.580146e-04 3.645558e-04
#> PCTGRT  0.0006580146 1.136777e-02 3.109028e-06
#> PCTSUPP 0.0003645558 3.109028e-06 9.783594e-03
stats::vcov(object = adf)
#>              NARTIC       PCTGRT      PCTSUPP
#> NARTIC  0.010008319 0.0025897215 0.0021423294
#> PCTGRT  0.002589721 0.0101780631 0.0008563851
#> PCTSUPP 0.002142329 0.0008563851 0.0106838539
stats::vcov(object = hc3)
#>              NARTIC       PCTGRT      PCTSUPP
#> NARTIC  0.014020632 0.0036807534 0.0029199035
#> PCTGRT  0.003680753 0.0132272021 0.0009992982
#> PCTSUPP 0.002919904 0.0009992982 0.0129621009

confint

Return confidence intervals.

stats::confint(object = mvn, level = 0.95)
#>              2.5 %    97.5 %
#> NARTIC  0.24404271 0.6546911
#> PCTGRT  0.14898177 0.5601978
#> PCTSUPP 0.04855312 0.4257944
stats::confint(object = adf, level = 0.95)
#>             2.5 %    97.5 %
#> NARTIC  0.2389386 0.6329057
#> PCTGRT  0.1449664 0.5355016
#> PCTSUPP 0.0363954 0.4339313
stats::confint(object = hc3, level = 0.95)
#>              2.5 %    97.5 %
#> NARTIC  0.18140198 0.6482142
#> PCTGRT  0.10730870 0.5532402
#> PCTSUPP 0.02483994 0.4579576

References

Dudgeon, P. (2017). Some improvements in confidence intervals for standardized regression coefficients. Psychometrika, 82(4), 928–951. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11336-017-9563-z
Pesigan, I. J. A., & Cheung, S. F. (2024). Monte Carlo confidence intervals for the indirect effect with missing data. Behavior Research Methods, 56(3), 1678–1696. https://doi.org/10.3758/s13428-023-02114-4
